Current translation (msgstr): Utilise ce code pour rétablir tes données si tu perds l'accès à tes appareils. Garde-le en lieu sûr.
Issue: Two newly added French translations use informal "tu" form (`"Utilise ce code pour rétablir tes données si tu perds..."`, `"Tes paramètres sont enregistrés... Installe l'extension..."`) while the rest of the file consistently uses formal "vous" form. The nearly identical string at line 22368 correctly uses "vous" (`"Utilisez ce code pour restaurer vos discussions..."`), making the inconsistency especially visible for the recovery code message.

Issue: The newly added translation has two spaces before the colon: `et scannez ce code :` — French typography requires exactly one space before a colon, not two. This will be visible to users as an extra whitespace gap.

Source string (msgid): ... or ask a follow-up with Duck.ai
Current translation (msgstr): … oppure chiedi un follow-up con Duck.ai
Issue: The two newly added Italian translations for the follow-up prompt placeholder use different ellipsis characters. The mobile variant (line 573) uses three ASCII periods (`...`) matching the source `msgid`, while the desktop variant (line 578) uses a Unicode ellipsis (`…` U+2026). Since both are variants of the same AI Chat prompt input (mobile vs desktop widths for the same experiment), users may notice a visual inconsistency between viewports.

Context (msgctxt): Instruction in the mobile Scan-or-Copy-Code modal
Source string (msgid): Go to %sDuck.ai Settings%s in your other browser, or the DuckDuckGo App and go to %sChats › Sync & Backup › Sync With Another Device%s and scan this code:

Issue: The Italian translation for the mobile "Scan-or-Copy-Code" instruction is missing the conjunction `"e"` (meaning "and") between `"DuckDuckGo"` and `"vai su"`. The English source says "...the DuckDuckGo App **and** go to..." but this variant translates it as `"...DuckDuckGo vai su..."` instead of `"...DuckDuckGo e vai su..."`. The other three closely related "Go to" instruction translations all correctly include the `"e"`, making this an inconsistency in user-facing setup instructions.

Context (msgctxt): Instruction in the mobile Scan-or-Copy-Code modal

Issue: The Estonian translation for the mobile Scan-or-Copy-Code instruction uses `võime` ("we can") instead of `mine` ("go"), making the sentence grammatically incorrect and nonsensical. The three parallel translations of the same "Go to…" pattern at lines 8903, 8914, and 8937 all correctly use `või mine DuckDuckGo rakenduses`, confirming this is a typo.

The new translation for `"Switched to %s"` (a confirmation label shown after the model switch completes) is `"Beralih ke %1$s"`, which is identical to the button label `"Switch to %s"` also translated as `"Beralih ke %1$s"`. Indonesian uses markers like "Sudah" or "Telah" to express completed actions, so the confirmation label loses its distinction from the action button, potentially confusing users about whether the switch actually happened.

Source string (msgid): ... or ask a follow-up with Duck.ai
Current translation (msgstr): … или задайте последващ въпрос с Duck.ai
Issue: The translation for `"... or ask a follow-up"` at line 577 correctly uses three ASCII dots (`...`) matching the source `msgid`, but the closely related translation for `"... or ask a follow-up with Duck.ai"` at line 582 uses a Unicode horizontal ellipsis (`…` / U+2026) instead. Both source strings in `duckduckgo.pot` use ASCII `...`. This mismatch between two translations that serve as variants of the same UI element (one for narrow mobile, one for wider viewports) could cause visual inconsistency.

Two sibling translations for the same UI element use different ellipsis representations. Line 571 uses three ASCII period characters (`...`) while line 576 uses a single Unicode ellipsis (`…`). Both source `msgid` strings use `...` (three ASCII periods). These strings are viewport-width variants of the same AI Chat prompt input placeholder, so the visual inconsistency could be noticeable to users switching between mobile and desktop.

Context (msgctxt): Title for the joiner-device success screen
Issue: The `%1$s` placeholder in `"New device added to %sSync & Backup."` represents a line break (per the translator comment: "%s is a line break so the title wraps after 'to'"). The Turkish translation places `%1$s` at the very start of the string (`"%1$sSync & Backup'a yeni cihaz eklendi."`), which inserts a line break before any visible text — producing an empty first line. Other locales like Afrikaans correctly position it mid-string before "Sync & Backup".
